text:
Jamal Ortiz: hey team, new here — trying to finish kube access. I merged the company kubeconfig with my home one and now `kubectl` errors with TLS: "x509: certificate is valid for kubernetes.default, not dev.reds.internal". Anyone seen this?

DevEx Bot: welcome Jamal! :wave: That message usually means the server certificate CN/SANs don't match the hostname you're hitting. Quick checks:
• run `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.clusters[0].cluster.server}'` to see the exact server URL
• verify VPN/proxy isn't rewriting the host header
• if you have `kubectl` hitting a cluster via a load-balancer IP, the cert may be for an internal DNS name

Jamal Ortiz: server is `https://10.18.5.42:6443` (I think this is the node IP?). The onboard kubeconfig had `server: https://dev.reds.internal:6443`. I must have merged wrong entries.

Nina R.: yup if your kubeconfig points to the node IP instead of the LB/DNS the cert mismatch happens. Use the cluster entry which has `server: https://dev.reds.internal:6443` and `certificate-authority-data`. If you have multiple clusters with same name, rename contexts instead of merging blindly.

Jamal Ortiz: how do I pick the right cluster entry without losing my personal contexts?

Nina R.: keep your personal config separate. Example: `export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:~/work/onboard/onboard-kubeconfig.yaml` then run `kubectl config view --flatten --merge > ~/.kube/merged && mv ~/.kube/merged ~/.kube/config` only after you confirm `kubectl config get-contexts` shows the `onboard` context with server `dev.reds.internal`. Or just use `kubectl --kubeconfig=~/work/onboard/onboard-kubeconfig.yaml get ns` while onboarding.

Jamal Ortiz: ok i switched back to the onboard file and `kubectl get ns` works when on VPN. When off VPN I get the cert error — guess the DNS doesn't resolve.

Infra Oncall: @Jamal that's expected — `dev.reds.internal` only resolves via our internal DNS over VPN. If you need remote dev access use the bastion jump or the cloud dev endpoint we provision for remote workers. I can open a ticket to add a public egress LB if your team needs it long-term.

Jamal Ortiz: perfect, thanks. One more question: after merging I saw duplicate users in `kubectl config view users` (one token-based, one oidc). Which one does kubectl pick?

DevEx Bot: kubectl picks the user referenced by the active context (see `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.contexts[0].context.user}'`). If the context points to `jamal@company` (oidc) then the token user is ignored. Cleanest approach: rename contexts and keep company kubeconfigs separate until you finish onboarding.

Jamal Ortiz: thanks all — VPN + onboard kubeconfig + correct context fixed it. Appreciate the quick help :muscle:

Nina R.: welcome aboard Jamal! I'll add a short note in the onboarding doc about DNS vs IP and cert SAN mismatches.

DevEx Bot: noted — helpful tip: avoid rewriting `~/.kube/config` until you're sure. Use `--kubeconfig` or `KUBECONFIG` env var instead.
